claim: Both the Amazon Route 53 authoritative service and the Amazon Route 53 Resolver Endpoints service offer a service credit if a customer's monthly uptime percentage falls below the service commitment in a billing cycle.
question: Does Route 53 have an SLA, and which Route 53 services does it cover?

qualifiers.scope: Route 53 authoritative service and Resolver Endpoints service
qualifiers.condition: monthly uptime percentage below the service commitment

evidence.quote: Both the Amazon Route 53 authoritative service and the Amazon Route 53 Resolver Endpoints service provide for a service credit if a customer’s monthly uptime percentage is below our service commitment in any billing cycle.

claim: For the Route 53 SLA, a hosted zone is unavailable in a given minute only if all four virtual name servers assigned to it fail to respond to all DNS queries throughout that minute.
question: When does the Route 53 SLA count a hosted zone as unavailable?

evidence.quote: A Hosted Zone is “Unavailable” during a given minute if all four virtual name servers assigned to the Hosted Zone fail to respond to all DNS queries made to the Hosted Zone throughout the minute.

claim: Under the Route 53 SLA for a hosted zone outside GovCloud, a monthly uptime percentage of less than 100% but at least 99.99% earns a service credit of 10% of the query charges.
question: What service credit does the Route 53 SLA give when monthly uptime is less than 100% but at least 99.99%?

values.display: less than 100% but greater than or equal to 99.99%

qualifiers.scope: per hosted zone, per monthly billing cycle, outside GovCloud
qualifiers.condition: credit is a percentage of Route 53 query charges for the affected hosted zone

evidence.quote: | Less than 100% but greater than or equal to 99.99% | 10% |
evidence.table_header: | Monthly Uptime Percentage for a Hosted Zone (other than a Hosted Zone in a GovCloud region) | Service Credit Percentage |

claim: Amazon Route 53 uses anycast, a networking and routing technology that helps DNS queries get answered from the optimal Route 53 location given network conditions.
question: Does Route 53 use an anycast network, and what does it do?

evidence.quote: Anycast is a networking and routing technology that helps your end users’ DNS queries get answered from the optimal Route 53 location given network conditions.

claim: Using a global anycast network of DNS servers, Route 53 is designed to answer queries automatically from the optimal location depending on network conditions, which gives low query latency.
question: How does Route 53 provide high availability and low latency?

values.display: global anycast network of DNS servers

evidence.quote: Using a global anycast network of DNS servers around the world, Route 53 is designed to automatically answer queries from the optimal location depending on network conditions.
As a result, the service offers low query latency for your end users.

claim: An alias record can map the zone apex to a load balancer, and Route 53 supports alias records for three types of load balancers: Application, Network and Classic.
question: Can the zone apex point at an Elastic Load Balancer, and which load balancer types work with an alias record?

evidence.quote: Route 53 supports alias records for three types of load balancers: Application Load Balancers, Network Load Balancers, and Classic Load Balancers.
IP addresses associated with load balancers can change at any time due to scaling up, scaling down, or software updates.

claim: An alias record can map the zone apex to an Amazon S3 website bucket, and Route 53 answers each request with one IP address for the bucket.
question: Can the zone apex point at a website hosted on Amazon S3?

values.display: zone apex (example.com) DNS name to your Amazon S3 website bucket

qualifiers.scope: alias records to S3 website buckets

evidence.quote: Amazon Route 53 offers a special type of record called an ‘Alias’ record that lets you map your zone apex (example.com) DNS name to your Amazon S3 website bucket (i.e. example.com.s3-website-us-west-2.amazonaws.com).
Route 53 responds to each request for an Alias record with one IP address for the bucket.

claim: An alias record can map the zone apex to an Amazon CloudFront distribution.
question: Can the zone apex point at an Amazon CloudFront distribution?

values.display: zone apex (example.com) DNS name to your Amazon CloudFront distribution

evidence.quote: Amazon Route 53 offers a special type of record called an ‘Alias’ record that lets you map your zone apex (example.com) DNS name to your Amazon CloudFront distribution (for example, d123.cloudfront.net).

claim: An alias record can map the zone apex to an Amazon API Gateway DNS name.
question: Can the zone apex point at an Amazon API Gateway?

values.display: zone apex (example.com) DNS name to your Amazon API Gateway DNS name

evidence.quote: Amazon Route 53 offers a special type of record called an ‘Alias’ record that lets you map your zone apex (example.com) DNS name to your Amazon API Gateway DNS name (i.e. api-id.execute-api.region.amazonaws.com/stage).

claim: An alias record can map the zone apex to an Amazon VPC endpoint DNS name.
question: Can the zone apex point at an Amazon VPC endpoint?

values.display: zone apex (example.com) DNS name to your Amazon VPC Endpoint DNS name

evidence.quote: Amazon Route 53 offers a special type of record called an ‘Alias’ record that lets you map your zone apex (example.com) DNS name to your Amazon VPC Endpoint DNS name (i.e. vpce-svc-03d5ebb7d9579a2b3.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com).

claim: There is no additional charge for queries to alias records that are mapped to AWS ELB load balancers.
question: Is there a charge for Route 53 queries to alias records that point at ELB load balancers?

values.display: no additional charge for queries to Alias records

qualifiers.condition: queries are listed as Intra-AWS-DNS-Queries on the usage report

evidence.quote: There is no additional charge for queries to Alias records that are mapped to AWS ELB load balancers.
These queries are listed as “Intra-AWS-DNS-Queries” on the Amazon Route 53 usage report.

claim: Route 53 does not charge for queries to alias records that are mapped to a CloudFront distribution or to an S3 bucket configured as a website.
question: Is there a charge for Route 53 queries to alias records that point at CloudFront or an S3 website bucket?

values.display: doesn't charge for queries to Alias records

qualifiers.scope: alias records mapped to CloudFront or S3 website buckets

evidence.quote: Route 53 doesn't charge for queries to Alias records that are mapped to an S3 bucket that is configured as a website.
Route 53 doesn't charge for queries to Alias records that are mapped to a CloudFront distribution.

claim: Alias records have two advantages over CNAMEs: unlike a CNAME, an alias record can be created for the zone apex, and queries to alias records are free of charge.
question: What are the advantages of an alias record over a CNAME record?

values.display: queries to Alias records are free of charge

qualifiers.scope: alias records to CloudFront and S3 website buckets

evidence.quote: Alias records have two advantages: first, unlike CNAMEs, you can create an Alias record for your zone apex (e.g. example.com, instead of www.example.com), and second, queries to Alias records are free of charge.

claim: For CloudFront distributions and S3 buckets configured as static websites, AWS recommends an alias record instead of a CNAME.
question: Should you use an alias record or a CNAME for a CloudFront distribution or an S3 static website?

qualifiers.scope: CloudFront distributions and S3 website buckets

evidence.quote: For CloudFront distributions and S3 buckets configured to host static websites, we recommend creating an ‘Alias’ record that maps to your CloudFront distribution or S3 website bucket, instead of using CNAMEs.

claim: For an S3 bucket that is not configured to host a static website, you can create a CNAME record for your domain and the S3 bucket name.
question: Which record type do you use for an S3 bucket that is not set up as a static website?

qualifiers.scope: S3 buckets not configured as websites

evidence.quote: For S3 buckets not configured to host static websites, you can create a CNAME record for your domain and the S3 bucket name.

claim: To fully establish the alias between your domain name and an S3 bucket or CloudFront distribution, you must also configure the bucket or distribution with the alternate domain name entry.
question: Is a Route 53 record alone enough to point your domain name at a CloudFront distribution or an S3 bucket?

evidence.quote: In all cases, note that you will also need to configure your S3 bucket or your CloudFront distribution respectively with the alternate domain name entry to completely establish the alias between your domain name and the AWS domain name for your bucket or distribution.
